worlds.title: Caring for the World Around Us
worlds.sourceTitle: CARING FOR THE WORLD AROUND US

lessons.title: Truth Lights the Way
lessons.arabic: إِنَّ الصِّدْقَ يَهْدِي إِلَى الْبِرِّ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Being truthful leads us toward goodness.
lessons.explanation: Your words are powerful! Telling the truth builds trust, even when admitting a mistake feels difficult. Allah loves the path of goodness.
lessons.action: If you make a mistake today, tell a trusted adult the truth about it.
lessons.story: Imaan and Akhlaq are drawing a garden. Akhlaq reaches for a blue pencil and accidentally spills some water. Nobody else saw it. He takes a breath, tells Dadi Jaan what happened and asks how he can help clean up.
lessons.question: You accidentally knock over a cup. What is the honest choice?

answers.text: Blame someone else.
answers.feedback: Think about how the other person would feel. Try a choice that tells the truth.

answers.text: Tell a trusted adult what happened and offer to help.
answers.feedback: That is an honest, helpful choice. A mistake can be a chance to build trust.

answers.text: Hide the cup and walk away.
answers.feedback: Hiding it does not put things right. Who could you tell and ask for help?

lessons.title: A Promise Matters
lessons.arabic: إِذَا وَعَدَ أَخْلَفَ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Breaking a promise is a serious bad habit.
lessons.explanation: Our Prophet ﷺ warned us about breaking promises as a sign of hypocrisy. We learn the opposite habit: make promises carefully and try our best to keep them.
lessons.action: Keep one small promise you have made today.
lessons.story: Imaan promises to return Akhlaq’s storybook after lunch. Later, her friends invite her to play. She remembers her promise, returns the book first, and then joins the game. Akhlaq knows he can trust her words.
lessons.question: You promised to return a book today, but a game is starting. What could you do?

answers.text: Keep the book and hope your friend forgets.
answers.feedback: A promise matters even when another activity looks exciting. Try again.

answers.text: Make another promise without thinking about it.
answers.feedback: It helps to be careful about what we promise. Think about the promise you already made.

answers.text: Return it as promised, or honestly explain if you need help.
answers.feedback: You are taking your promise seriously. Honest communication helps protect trust.

lessons.title: Choose Kind Words
lessons.arabic: فَلْيَقُلْ خَيْرًا أَوْ لِيَصْمُتْ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Say what is good, or stay quiet.
lessons.explanation: Before speaking, ask: Is it true? Is it kind? Is it useful? Sometimes a quiet pause can protect another person’s heart.
lessons.action: Before replying in a difficult moment, pause and choose one kind sentence.
lessons.story: Akhlaq loses a turn in a game and feels upset. He is about to say something hurtful. Imaan gives him a moment. He pauses and says, “I’m disappointed. Can we try another round?” The game stays friendly.
lessons.question: A friend makes a mistake during a game. Which response is kind?

answers.text: “It’s okay. Let’s try again together.”
answers.feedback: Your words give your friend a safe chance to try again. A pause can help you choose them.

answers.text: Call your friend an unkind name.
answers.feedback: Names can hurt. Choose words that help instead.

answers.text: Say something mean because you feel annoyed.
answers.feedback: Feeling annoyed is understandable. You can pause before choosing what to say.

lessons.title: Safe Hands, Safe Words
lessons.arabic: الْمُسْلِمُ مَنْ سَلِمَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ مِنْ لِسَانِهِ وَيَدِهِ
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: A Muslim should not harm others with words or hands.
lessons.explanation: Being strong is not about pushing or teasing. It means making people feel safe around you.
lessons.action: During play today, keep your hands gentle and your words respectful.
lessons.story: Two children both want the same ball. Akhlaq feels like grabbing it. He keeps his hands gentle and asks for a turn. Imaan suggests taking turns, so everyone can play without being pushed or teased.
lessons.question: Someone is using the toy you want. What is a safe choice?

answers.text: Push them and take it.
answers.feedback: Pushing can hurt someone. Choose a way that keeps their body safe.

answers.text: Ask politely for a turn and keep your hands gentle.
answers.feedback: That protects the other person with both your hands and your words.

answers.text: Tease them until they give it to you.
answers.feedback: Teasing can make someone feel unsafe too. Try a respectful request.

lessons.title: Beautiful Character
lessons.arabic: إِنَّ مِنْ خِيَارِكُمْ أَحْسَنَكُمْ أَخْلَاقًا
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Among the best people are those with the best character.
lessons.explanation: You do not need a medal to be wonderful. Your honesty, patience and kindness make a real difference!
lessons.action: Choose one moment today to respond with extra politeness.
lessons.story: Imaan is busy making a paper flower when her little cousin asks for help. She puts it down for a moment and answers gently. Akhlaq notices that beautiful character can show itself in one small, ordinary choice.
lessons.question: A younger child asks you for help while you are busy. What shows good character?

answers.text: Laugh at them for not knowing.
answers.feedback: We all need help sometimes. Look for a more caring choice.

answers.text: Shout at them to go away.
answers.feedback: You can set a limit kindly without shouting. Think about how you could speak politely.

answers.text: Answer politely and help, or kindly say when you can help.
answers.feedback: Kindness and politeness matter in everyday moments, even when you are busy.

lessons.title: Wish Good for Others
lessons.arabic: لاَ يُؤْمِنُ أَحَدُكُمْ حَتَّى يُحِبَّ لأَخِيهِ مَا يُحِبُّ لِنَفْسِهِ
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: Love for others the good you love for yourself.
lessons.explanation: You enjoy being welcomed and included. Other children do too! A caring heart wants goodness for everyone.
lessons.action: Invite one child to join a game or activity.
lessons.story: Imaan is picking teams for a game. A new girl stands by the wall, watching. Imaan remembers how good it feels to be chosen. She walks over and says, “Would you like to play on our team?”
lessons.question: A child is standing alone while everyone else plays. What could you do?

answers.text: Invite them to join the game.
answers.feedback: You want for them the same welcome you would want for yourself. That is a caring heart.

answers.text: Ignore them because they are new.
answers.feedback: Being new can feel lonely. Think about how you would want to be treated.

answers.text: Tell them the game is full, even though it is not.
answers.feedback: That is not true, and it leaves them out. Try a more welcoming choice.

lessons.title: A Merciful Heart
lessons.arabic: مَنْ لاَ يَرْحَمُ لاَ يُرْحَمُ
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: Whoever shows no mercy is not shown mercy.
lessons.explanation: Mercy means noticing when someone is sad, small, frightened or struggling—and treating them gently.
lessons.action: Comfort someone who looks upset today.
lessons.story: Akhlaq sees his little cousin crying after falling off a swing. Some children laugh. Akhlaq kneels down, asks if he is hurt, and helps him find an adult. His cousin stops crying and holds his hand.
lessons.question: A younger child falls and starts to cry. What shows a merciful heart?

answers.text: Laugh along with the others.
answers.feedback: Laughing can make the hurt feel worse. Look for a gentler choice.

answers.text: Check that they are okay and get help if needed.
answers.feedback: You noticed their pain and treated them gently. That is mercy.

answers.text: Walk away because it is not your problem.
answers.feedback: Mercy means noticing when someone is struggling. How could you help?

lessons.title: Words Can Be Charity
lessons.arabic: وَالْكَلِمَةُ الطَّيِّبَةُ صَدَقَةٌ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: A good word is an act of charity.
lessons.explanation: You can give a beautiful gift even without money: kind words! They make others feel noticed and appreciated.
lessons.action: Give one sincere compliment to someone today.
lessons.story: Imaan’s friend shows a drawing she worked hard on. It is a little messy, but the colours are bright. Imaan says, “I love the colours you chose!” Her friend smiles all the way home.
lessons.question: Your classmate shows you their project. What could you say?

answers.text: Say nothing and look away.
answers.feedback: A kind word can be a gift. Could you find something good to say?

answers.text: Point out every mistake loudly.
answers.feedback: Pointing out mistakes in front of others can hurt. Try a kind word first.

answers.text: Give one sincere compliment about something you like.
answers.feedback: A true, kind word is a beautiful gift that costs nothing.

lessons.title: A Cheerful Welcome
lessons.arabic: لاَ تَحْقِرَنَّ مِنَ الْمَعْرُوفِ شَيْئًا وَلَوْ أَنْ تَلْقَى أَخَاكَ بِوَجْهٍ طَلْقٍ
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: Even a cheerful greeting is a meaningful good deed.
lessons.explanation: A smile and friendly face can make a new child feel that they belong. Little good deeds matter to Allah.
lessons.action: Welcome someone today with a warm greeting and cheerful face.
lessons.story: A new boy joins Akhlaq’s class and looks nervous. Akhlaq remembers that a small good deed still matters. He smiles, says Assalamu Alaikum, and shows him where to hang his bag.
lessons.question: A new child arrives at your class. What is a small good deed you could do?

answers.text: Greet them with a warm smile.
answers.feedback: A cheerful face helps someone feel they belong. Small good deeds matter.

answers.text: Stare at them without saying anything.
answers.feedback: Staring can feel uncomfortable. How could you make them feel welcome?

answers.text: Whisper about them with friends.
answers.feedback: Whispering about someone can make them feel left out. Try a friendly greeting.

lessons.title: Kindness to Animals
lessons.arabic: فِي كُلِّ كَبِدٍ رَطْبَةٍ أَجْرٌ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: There is reward in kindness to living creatures.
lessons.explanation: Animals feel thirst and need care. Our faith teaches compassion for living things, not just for people.
lessons.action: With an adult’s help, safely place clean water where birds can drink.
lessons.story: On a hot afternoon, Imaan notices birds hopping near the dry garden tap. She asks Ammi for help, and together they place a shallow bowl of clean water in a safe, shady spot. Soon a sparrow comes to drink.
lessons.question: You see a thirsty bird on a hot day. What is a kind and safe choice?

answers.text: Chase it away for fun.
answers.feedback: Animals feel thirst and fear too. Think of a gentle choice.

answers.text: Ask an adult to help you put out some clean water.
answers.feedback: That is compassion for a living creature, done safely with an adult.

answers.text: Throw small stones near it.
answers.feedback: That could hurt or frighten the bird. Our faith teaches kindness to animals.

lessons.title: Be Your Best at Home
lessons.arabic: خَيْرُكُمْ خَيْرُكُمْ لِأَهْلِهِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: The best of you are those best to their families.
lessons.explanation: Good manners begin at home. Family members deserve the same cheerful kindness that we show visitors and friends.
lessons.action: Offer to help a family member with one task without being asked.
lessons.story: After school, Akhlaq is polite to his friends but grumpy at home. Then he notices Baba carrying heavy shopping bags. He jumps up, takes one bag, and says, “Let me help.” Baba smiles warmly.
lessons.question: Your family member is busy with a task. What shows your best at home?

answers.text: Offer to help without being asked.
answers.feedback: Good manners begin at home. Your family deserves your kindness too.

answers.text: Keep playing and pretend not to notice.
answers.feedback: Your family needs your kindness as much as your friends do. Try again.

answers.text: Help only if they give you a prize.
answers.feedback: Helping at home is a gift of love, not a trade. What could you do freely?

lessons.title: Greet Your Elders
lessons.arabic: يُسَلِّمُ الصَّغِيرُ عَلَى الْكَبِيرِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: A younger person should offer salam to an older person.
lessons.explanation: You can begin a beautiful moment with one greeting. Saying salam shows respect and spreads peace.
lessons.action: Say Assalamu Alaikum first to an elder today.
lessons.story: Dada Abbu visits for dinner. Imaan is busy with her puzzle, but she stops, walks over, and says, “Assalamu Alaikum, Dada Abbu!” He smiles and pats her head.
lessons.question: An elder relative enters the room. What could you do first?

answers.text: Wait for them to greet you.
answers.feedback: You can be the one to begin. Think about who greets first.

answers.text: Keep looking at your screen.
answers.feedback: Elders deserve your attention and respect. Try another choice.

answers.text: Say Assalamu Alaikum to them first.
answers.feedback: A greeting from you shows respect and spreads peace.

lessons.title: Love and Care for Mother
lessons.arabic: أُمُّكَ ثُمَّ أُمُّكَ ثُمَّ أُمُّكَ ثُمَّ أَبُوكَ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Your mother deserves special good companionship, and your father also deserves it.
lessons.explanation: Our parents work hard to care for us. We can answer their care with respect, gratitude and gentle words.
lessons.action: Say a heartfelt thank-you to your mother or caregiver today.
lessons.story: Ammi is tired after a long day. Akhlaq notices and brings her a glass of water. He says, “Thank you for everything you do for us, Ammi.” Her tired face lights up with a smile.
lessons.question: Your mother or caregiver looks tired. What is a caring response?

answers.text: Ask for more snacks right away.
answers.feedback: She is tired right now. How could you show care instead?

answers.text: Thank her and offer a little help.
answers.feedback: Gratitude and gentle care honour the people who look after us.

answers.text: Complain that dinner is late.
answers.feedback: Complaining can add to her tiredness. Try a kinder choice.

lessons.title: The Prophet Helped at Home
lessons.arabic: كَانَ يَكُونُ فِي مِهْنَةِ أَهْلِهِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ helped and served his family at home.
lessons.explanation: Aishah (رضي الله عنها) described how the Prophet ﷺ helped his family. Helping at home is noble, not something to avoid.
lessons.action: Put away your own belongings today without waiting to be reminded.
lessons.story: Imaan’s toys are spread across the living room floor. Nobody has asked her to tidy up yet. She remembers that helping at home is a noble thing, and she puts every toy back in its box.
lessons.question: Your things are lying around the house. What could you do?

answers.text: Leave them for someone else to pick up.
answers.feedback: Helping at home is something to be proud of, not avoid. Try again.

answers.text: Put them away without being reminded.
answers.feedback: That is real help at home. You are taking care of your family’s space.

answers.text: Hide them under the sofa.
answers.feedback: Hiding things does not really tidy them. What would truly help?

lessons.title: Stay Connected to Family
lessons.arabic: فَلْيَصِلْ رَحِمَهُ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Keep your family ties strong.
lessons.explanation: Family love grows when we remember and care for relatives. A short greeting can brighten someone’s whole day.
lessons.action: With a parent’s help, send a greeting to a relative today.
lessons.story: Akhlaq’s Khala lives in another city. He has not spoken to her for a long time. With Ammi’s help, he records a short voice message: “Assalamu Alaikum, Khala! I miss you.” She replies with a happy message.
lessons.question: You have not spoken to a relative for a while. What could you do?

answers.text: With a parent’s help, send them a greeting.
answers.feedback: A short greeting keeps family ties strong and can brighten their day.

answers.text: Wait until they contact you.
answers.feedback: You can be the one who reaches out. How could you connect?

answers.text: Forget about them because they live far away.
answers.feedback: Family love can grow even across distance. Try a caring choice.

lessons.title: Pause Before Anger
lessons.arabic: لاَ تَغْضَبْ
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: Do not give in to anger.
lessons.explanation: Feeling angry can happen to anyone. The challenge is choosing what to do next instead of shouting or hurting.
lessons.action: When upset today, stop and take three slow breaths before replying.
lessons.story: Akhlaq’s little brother knocks over his block tower. Akhlaq feels his face get hot. He stops, takes three slow breaths, and then says, “Please be careful. Let’s build it again together.”
lessons.question: Someone ruins something you made. What could you do first?

answers.text: Shout at them right away.
answers.feedback: Feeling angry is normal, but shouting can hurt. What could you do first?

answers.text: Knock over something of theirs.
answers.feedback: Getting even does not fix things. Try a calmer choice.

answers.text: Stop and take a few slow breaths before speaking.
answers.feedback: Pausing gives you a chance to choose your next step wisely.

lessons.title: Real Strength
lessons.arabic: إِنَّمَا الشَّدِيدُ الَّذِي يَمْلِكُ نَفْسَهُ عِنْدَ الْغَضَبِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: The truly strong person controls themself when angry.
lessons.explanation: You are stronger when you can calm your voice than when you win an argument. Self-control is a real superpower.
lessons.action: In one frustrating moment today, lower your voice instead of raising it.
lessons.story: During a board game, Imaan’s friend says she cheated, which is not true. Imaan feels like yelling. Instead she lowers her voice and says, “I didn’t cheat. Let’s check the rules together.”
lessons.question: Someone says something unfair to you during a game. What shows real strength?

answers.text: Shout louder until they stop.
answers.feedback: Being loud is not the same as being strong. Try another way.

answers.text: Keep your voice calm and explain.
answers.feedback: Controlling yourself when you are angry is real strength.

answers.text: Throw the game pieces.
answers.feedback: That could hurt someone or spoil the game. What would a strong person do?

lessons.title: Be Patient at the Start
lessons.arabic: إِنَّمَا الصَّبْرُ عِنْدَ الصَّدْمَةِ الأُولَى
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: Real patience shows itself at the first difficult moment.
lessons.explanation: A disappointment can feel big at first. You can pause, ask Allah for help, and choose a calmer next step.
lessons.action: When one plan changes today, respond without complaining for one minute.
lessons.story: Akhlaq was looking forward to the park, but it starts to rain. His first feeling is to complain. He pauses, says a quiet du’a, and suggests a board game indoors instead.
lessons.question: Your plan is suddenly cancelled. What shows patience?

answers.text: Pause, stay calm and look for another idea.
answers.feedback: Real patience shows itself at the first difficult moment. Well done.

answers.text: Complain loudly for the rest of the day.
answers.feedback: It is okay to feel disappointed. How could you respond more calmly?

answers.text: Blame someone for the change.
answers.feedback: Sometimes plans change and nobody is to blame. Try a calmer step.

lessons.title: Choose Gentleness
lessons.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ رَفِيقٌ يُحِبُّ الرِّفْقَ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Allah is gentle and loves gentleness.
lessons.explanation: Your gentle voice can calm a younger child or help settle a disagreement. Kindness can be firm without being harsh.
lessons.action: Speak gently to someone who needs your help today.
lessons.story: Imaan’s little sister is struggling to tie her shoes and starts to get upset. Imaan sits beside her and speaks softly: “Let’s do it slowly together.” Her sister calms down and tries again.
lessons.question: A younger child is upset and needs your help. How could you speak?

answers.text: Speak harshly so they hurry up.
answers.feedback: Harsh words can make it harder. Think of a gentler way.

answers.text: Use a gentle voice and help patiently.
answers.feedback: Gentleness can calm someone and help them learn.

answers.text: Laugh because they are slow.
answers.feedback: Laughing can hurt their feelings. Try a kinder response.

lessons.title: Gentleness Makes Things Beautiful
lessons.arabic: إِنَّ الرِّفْقَ لاَ يَكُونُ فِي شَيْءٍ إِلاَّ زَانَهُ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Gentleness makes things better and more beautiful.
lessons.explanation: Think of how much easier it is to learn when someone patiently explains. Your gentleness can help others learn too.
lessons.action: Explain one thing patiently to someone who does not understand it yet.
lessons.story: Akhlaq’s friend cannot understand a maths question. Akhlaq could just give him the answer, but instead he explains it step by step, patiently. Soon his friend says, “Oh, now I get it!”
lessons.question: A friend does not understand something you know. What is the gentle choice?

answers.text: Say “That’s easy, why don’t you get it?”
answers.feedback: That can make your friend feel silly. Try a gentler way.

answers.text: Refuse to help.
answers.feedback: Your help could make a big difference. What could you do?

answers.text: Explain it slowly and patiently.
answers.feedback: Gentleness makes learning easier and more beautiful.

lessons.title: Thank People
lessons.arabic: مَنْ لاَ يَشْكُرِ النَّاسَ لاَ يَشْكُرِ اللَّهَ
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: Gratitude to people is part of gratitude to Allah.
lessons.explanation: Someone cooked, taught, cleaned or helped you today. Notice their effort and let them know it matters.
lessons.action: Thank one person for a specific helpful thing they did.
lessons.story: The school cleaner, Uncle Rashid, always keeps the classroom tidy. One morning, Imaan stops and says, “Thank you for keeping our classroom so clean!” He smiles and says it made his day.
lessons.question: Someone helped you today. What could you do?

answers.text: Thank them for the specific thing they did.
answers.feedback: Noticing someone’s effort and thanking them is a beautiful habit.

answers.text: Say nothing because it is their job.
answers.feedback: Everyone’s effort deserves to be noticed. Could you show gratitude?

answers.text: Thank them only if others are watching.
answers.feedback: Gratitude is sincere, whoever is watching. Try again.

lessons.title: Grateful in Happy Times
lessons.arabic: إِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ سَرَّاءُ شَكَرَ فَكَانَ خَيْرًا لَهُ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: When something good happens, a believer gives thanks.
lessons.explanation: Happy moments are chances to remember Allah. Gratitude helps us enjoy blessings without forgetting the One who gives them.
lessons.action: When something good happens today, say Alhamdulillah sincerely.
lessons.story: Akhlaq finds out he did well on his spelling test. He feels so happy! Before running to tell his friends, he quietly says, “Alhamdulillah,” remembering who gave him the ability to learn.
lessons.question: Something good happens to you. What is a grateful response?

answers.text: Show off to everyone.
answers.feedback: Being happy is good, but showing off can make others feel bad. Try again.

answers.text: Say Alhamdulillah sincerely.
answers.feedback: Remembering Allah in happy moments is a beautiful kind of gratitude.

answers.text: Forget about it straight away.
answers.feedback: Good moments are chances to remember Allah. What could you say?

lessons.title: Notice Your Blessings
lessons.arabic: انْظُرُوا إِلَى مَنْ أَسْفَلَ مِنْكُمْ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Look at those who have less than you in worldly things.
lessons.explanation: Rather than comparing your things with someone who has more, notice the gifts Allah has already given you.
lessons.action: Name one everyday blessing you often forget to appreciate.
lessons.story: Imaan feels sad because her friend has a fancier pencil case. Then she thinks about her own warm home, her family and her lunch box. She feels thankful for the gifts Allah has already given her.
lessons.question: You feel upset because a friend has something nicer. What helps?

answers.text: Keep comparing until you feel worse.
answers.feedback: Comparing with those who have more can steal our happiness. Try another thought.

answers.text: Take their pencil case.
answers.feedback: Taking what is not yours is never right. What could help your heart instead?

answers.text: Notice the blessings you already have.
answers.feedback: Looking at your own blessings helps your heart feel grateful.

lessons.title: Small Habits Grow
lessons.arabic: أَحَبَّ الأَعْمَالِ أَدْوَمُهَا إِلَى اللَّهِ وَإِنْ قَلَّ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Allah loves good deeds done regularly, even when small.
lessons.explanation: One small good habit repeated daily can shape your character. Start small and keep going!
lessons.action: Spend two minutes revising a surah you already know today.
lessons.story: Akhlaq wants to learn a long surah all in one day. Dadi Jaan smiles and suggests two minutes every day instead. A week later, he still remembers his short surah perfectly.
lessons.question: You want to build a good habit. What works best?

answers.text: Do a small amount every day.
answers.feedback: Small good deeds done regularly can shape your character.

answers.text: Do a lot once and then stop.
answers.feedback: Big bursts are hard to keep up. What could you do regularly?

answers.text: Wait until you have lots of time.
answers.feedback: Small steps can start today. Try a steadier choice.

lessons.title: The Heart Matters
lessons.arabic: وَلَكِنْ يَنْظُرُ إِلَى قُلُوبِكُمْ وَأَعْمَالِكُمْ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Allah looks at your hearts and your actions.
lessons.explanation: Your clothes and possessions do not decide your worth. A sincere heart and good actions matter much more.
lessons.action: Do one helpful deed today without asking for praise.
lessons.story: Imaan helps her teacher carry books to the library. Nobody else sees it. She does not tell anyone, because she did it to help, not for praise. Her heart feels quietly happy.
lessons.question: You do something helpful but nobody notices. What matters most?

answers.text: Tell everyone so they praise you.
answers.feedback: Wanting praise is natural, but a sincere heart matters more. Try again.

answers.text: Stop helping because nobody saw.
answers.feedback: Allah sees your heart and your actions. Keep going!

answers.text: Your sincere heart and good action matter.
answers.feedback: You remembered that a sincere heart and good actions matter much more.

lessons.title: Cleanliness Is Important
lessons.arabic: الطُّهُورُ شَطْرُ الإِيمَانِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Purification is half of faith.
lessons.explanation: Cleanliness is part of our worship and everyday care. Keeping ourselves clean can be a beautiful habit.
lessons.action: Wash your hands properly before your next meal.
lessons.story: Akhlaq rushes in from playing football, ready to grab a samosa. He looks at his muddy hands, stops, and washes them properly with soap first. Then he enjoys his snack.
lessons.question: You are about to eat but your hands are dirty. What should you do?

answers.text: Wash your hands properly first.
answers.feedback: Cleanliness is part of our faith and everyday care. Well done.

answers.text: Wipe them on your clothes.
answers.feedback: That does not really clean them. What would be better?

answers.text: Eat quickly before anyone notices.
answers.feedback: Dirty hands can make you unwell. Try a cleaner choice.

lessons.title: Keep Pathways Safe
lessons.arabic: وَأَدْنَاهَا إِمَاطَةُ الأَذَى عَنِ الطَّرِيقِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Removing harm from a path is a branch of faith.
lessons.explanation: A safe path helps everyone. Even small acts of tidiness can become rewarding good deeds.
lessons.action: With adult supervision, move one harmless piece of litter into a bin.
lessons.story: On the way to the masjid, Imaan sees a banana peel on the path. Someone could slip! With Baba nearby, she picks it up and puts it in the bin.
lessons.question: You see something on a path that could make someone slip. What could you do?

answers.text: Step over it and keep walking.
answers.feedback: Others might not see it. How could you keep the path safe?

answers.text: Kick it into the road.
answers.feedback: That moves the problem somewhere else. Try a safer choice.

answers.text: With an adult nearby, move it safely into a bin.
answers.feedback: Removing harm from a path helps everyone and is a good deed.

lessons.title: Beautiful and Clean
lessons.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ جَمِيلٌ يُحِبُّ الْجَمَالَ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Allah is beautiful and loves beauty.
lessons.explanation: Beauty is not about expensive things. Caring for neatness and treating others well makes our surroundings welcoming.
lessons.action: Tidy and arrange your study place today.
lessons.story: Akhlaq’s desk is covered in crumpled paper and broken crayons. It is hard to find anything. He tidies it, arranges his books neatly, and suddenly homework feels much easier.
lessons.question: Your study space is messy. What could you do?

answers.text: Leave it messy forever.
answers.feedback: A neat space can feel more welcoming. What could you change?

answers.text: Tidy and arrange it neatly.
answers.feedback: Caring for neatness makes our surroundings beautiful.

answers.text: Push everything onto the floor.
answers.feedback: That just moves the mess. Try a tidier choice.

lessons.title: Drink with Care
lessons.arabic: إِذَا شَرِبَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلاَ يَتَنَفَّسْ فِي الإِنَاءِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Do not breathe into the drinking vessel.
lessons.explanation: Small table manners protect hygiene and show consideration. Take a little pause away from the cup when you need a breath.
lessons.action: At your next drink, take the cup away from your mouth before breathing.
lessons.story: Imaan is very thirsty after playing. She gulps her water and nearly breathes into the cup. She remembers, lowers the cup, takes a breath, and then drinks again calmly.
lessons.question: You are drinking water and need to breathe. What is the polite way?

answers.text: Breathe into the cup.
answers.feedback: Small table manners protect hygiene. Try another way.

answers.text: Move the cup away from your mouth, then breathe.
answers.feedback: That is a clean and considerate habit.

answers.text: Blow bubbles into the water.
answers.feedback: That can be fun but is not hygienic for drinking. Try again.

lessons.title: A Polite Sneeze
lessons.arabic: إِذَا عَطَسَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَقُلِ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: When you sneeze, say Alhamdulillah.
lessons.explanation: Islam teaches beautiful everyday manners, even for ordinary moments. Remembering Allah can be part of your daily routine.
lessons.action: The next time you sneeze, cover your mouth appropriately and say Alhamdulillah.
lessons.story: In class, Akhlaq feels a sneeze coming. He covers his mouth with his elbow and then quietly says, “Alhamdulillah.” His friend next to him replies kindly.
lessons.question: You are about to sneeze. What is the polite thing to do?

answers.text: Sneeze into the air without covering.
answers.feedback: Covering your mouth protects others. Try a more polite way.

answers.text: Cover your mouth and say Alhamdulillah.
answers.feedback: You remembered Allah in an ordinary moment and protected others too.

answers.text: Pretend it never happened.
answers.feedback: There is a beautiful manner for sneezing. Can you remember it?

lessons.title: Begin with Allah’s Name
lessons.arabic: يَا غُلاَمُ سَمِّ اللَّهَ وَكُلْ بِيَمِينِكَ وَكُلْ مِمَّا يَلِيكَ
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: Say Allah’s name, eat with your right hand and eat from near you.
lessons.explanation: The Prophet ﷺ kindly taught a young boy how to eat. Simple manners can turn an ordinary meal into a chance to follow his example.
lessons.action: At your next meal, say Bismillah before you begin.
lessons.story: At a family lunch, Akhlaq is hungry and reaches for food from across the table. Then he remembers. He says Bismillah, uses his right hand, and eats from the side of the plate near him.
lessons.question: You are about to start your meal. What comes first?

answers.text: Say Bismillah before you begin.
answers.feedback: Saying Allah’s name turns an ordinary meal into a chance to follow the Sunnah.

answers.text: Grab food from the middle of the table.
answers.feedback: There are beautiful manners for eating. What could you do first?

answers.text: Start eating quickly without thinking.
answers.feedback: Slowing down helps you remember. What should you say first?

lessons.title: Eat with Balance
lessons.arabic: مَا مَلأَ آدَمِيٌّ وِعَاءً شَرًّا مِنْ بَطْنٍ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Avoid filling your stomach excessively.
lessons.explanation: Food is a blessing. Enjoy it calmly, and listen when your body tells you that you have had enough.
lessons.action: At one meal today, eat slowly and notice when you feel comfortably full.
lessons.story: There is biryani at Nani’s house, and Imaan loves it. She has a second plate and begins to feel full. She stops, puts her spoon down, and decides she has had enough.
lessons.question: You are eating your favourite food and feel full. What is a balanced choice?

answers.text: Keep eating until your tummy hurts.
answers.feedback: Food is a blessing, but too much can make us unwell. Try again.

answers.text: Hide food to eat later in secret.
answers.feedback: Hiding food is not needed. How could you listen to your body?

answers.text: Stop when you feel comfortably full.
answers.feedback: You listened to your body and enjoyed food with balance.

lessons.title: A Small Gift Counts
lessons.arabic: اتَّقُوا النَّارَ وَلَوْ بِشِقِّ تَمْرَةٍ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Even a very small gift of charity matters.
lessons.explanation: You do not need to be wealthy to be generous. A small gift, offered sincerely, can be special.
lessons.action: Share a small part of your snack with someone who would welcome it.
lessons.story: Akhlaq has a small packet of biscuits. His friend forgot his snack today. Akhlaq does not have much, but he shares two biscuits. His friend says it was the best biscuit ever.
lessons.question: You only have a small snack, and a friend has none. What could you do?

answers.text: Eat it all quickly before they see.
answers.feedback: Even a small share can be special. Think again.

answers.text: Share a small part with them.
answers.feedback: You do not need much to be generous. A small gift, given sincerely, counts.

answers.text: Tell them to buy their own.
answers.feedback: They might not be able to today. Try a more generous choice.

lessons.title: Respect the Food
lessons.arabic: مَا عَابَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ طَعَامًا قَطُّ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ never spoke badly about food.
lessons.explanation: You may not like every dish, and that is okay. We can decline politely without insulting the food or the person who prepared it.
lessons.action: If you dislike a food today, respond politely without mocking it.
lessons.story: Dadi Jaan cooks karela for dinner. Imaan does not like its bitter taste. Instead of making a face, she says, “Thank you, Dadi Jaan. Could I have a little less, please?”
lessons.question: You are served a food you do not like. What is the polite response?

answers.text: Say “Yuck, this is disgusting!”
answers.feedback: That can hurt the person who cooked. Try a polite way to decline.

answers.text: Politely take a little or decline without mocking it.
answers.feedback: You respected the food and the person who prepared it.

answers.text: Push the plate away rudely.
answers.feedback: There is a kinder way to show you do not want it. Try again.

lessons.title: Thank Allah After Eating
lessons.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَيَرْضَى عَنِ الْعَبْدِ أَنْ يَأْكُلَ الأَكْلَةَ فَيَحْمَدَهُ عَلَيْهَا
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Allah is pleased when a servant praises Him after eating.
lessons.explanation: Mealtimes bring nourishment, care and blessing. A simple Alhamdulillah helps you remember Allah’s generosity.
lessons.action: After your next meal, say Alhamdulillah with attention.
lessons.story: After a delicious meal, Akhlaq is ready to rush off and play. He stops for a moment and says, “Alhamdulillah,” thinking about who gave him the food. Then he thanks Ammi too.
lessons.question: You have just finished eating. What could you say?

answers.text: Say Alhamdulillah with attention.
answers.feedback: Praising Allah after eating helps you remember His generosity.

answers.text: Run off without a word.
answers.feedback: A meal is a blessing. What could you say before leaving?

answers.text: Complain that there was no dessert.
answers.feedback: Complaining can make us forget our blessings. Try again.

lessons.title: Help Each Other
lessons.arabic: وَاللَّهُ فِي عَوْنِ الْعَبْدِ مَا كَانَ الْعَبْدُ فِي عَوْنِ أَخِيهِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Allah helps the servant who helps another.
lessons.explanation: Someone in your class may need a helping hand. Helping sincerely is a lovely way to serve others.
lessons.action: Help one person complete a small task today.
lessons.story: Imaan’s classmate drops her crayons all over the floor. Some children giggle. Imaan kneels down and helps her pick them all up. Her classmate whispers, “Thank you.”
lessons.question: Someone drops their things. What could you do?

answers.text: Laugh with the others.
answers.feedback: Laughing can make them feel embarrassed. How could you help?

answers.text: Walk past quickly.
answers.feedback: Your help could make a difference. Try again.

answers.text: Help them pick things up.
answers.feedback: Helping someone sincerely is a lovely way to serve others.

lessons.title: Show Someone a Good Way
lessons.arabic: مَنْ دَلَّ عَلَى خَيْرٍ فَلَهُ مِثْلُ أَجْرِ فَاعِلِهِ
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: Guiding someone toward good brings a reward too.
lessons.explanation: You can help others discover a good habit, a useful book or a kind action. Goodness grows when shared.
lessons.action: Teach a friend one useful good habit you practise.
lessons.story: Akhlaq has learnt to say Bismillah before eating. He gently reminds his younger cousin at lunch, not to boss him, but to share something good. His cousin starts saying it too.
lessons.question: You know a good habit. What could you do with it?

answers.text: Keep it a secret.
answers.feedback: Goodness grows when it is shared. What could you do?

answers.text: Teach it kindly to a friend.
answers.feedback: Guiding someone toward good is a beautiful thing to do.

answers.text: Tease others for not knowing it.
answers.feedback: Teasing pushes people away. Try sharing it gently.

lessons.title: Every Good Deed Matters
lessons.arabic: كُلُّ مَعْرُوفٍ صَدَقَةٌ
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: Every good action is charity.
lessons.explanation: Opening a door, helping a friend or speaking kindly can all count. There are many ways to do good every day!
lessons.action: Do one small helpful deed for someone today.
lessons.story: Imaan holds the door for a lady carrying a baby. Later she helps her friend find a lost sock and says something kind to her brother. Little by little, her day is full of good deeds.
lessons.question: Which of these could count as a good deed?

answers.text: Holding a door open for someone.
answers.feedback: Yes! Even small kind actions can count as good deeds.

answers.text: Only very big, expensive things.
answers.feedback: Good deeds do not need to be big. Look again.

answers.text: Nothing, unless someone gives you a prize.
answers.feedback: Good deeds are not about prizes. Try again.

lessons.title: Be There for Someone
lessons.arabic: وَمَنْ كَانَ فِي حَاجَةِ أَخِيهِ كَانَ اللَّهُ فِي حَاجَتِهِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Allah helps those who look after another person’s needs.
lessons.explanation: If a friend needs help, do not always wait for someone else. Even a little assistance can make a big difference.
lessons.action: Offer appropriate help to a classmate who is struggling with a task.
lessons.story: Akhlaq’s classmate is struggling to carry a heavy art project. Others think someone else will help. Akhlaq does not wait. He holds one side and they carry it together.
lessons.question: A classmate is struggling with a task. What could you do?

answers.text: Wait for someone else to help.
answers.feedback: Sometimes nobody else steps in. Could you help?

answers.text: Offer a helping hand.
answers.feedback: Looking after someone’s need is a caring choice.

answers.text: Laugh because it looks funny.
answers.feedback: Struggling is not funny for them. Try a kinder response.

lessons.title: Care for People in Need
lessons.arabic: السَّاعِي عَلَى الأَرْمَلَةِ وَالْمِسْكِينِ كَالْمُجَاهِدِ فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Caring for people in need has a tremendous reward.
lessons.explanation: A caring community remembers people who have less support. Children can learn compassion through simple, safe acts of giving.
lessons.action: With an adult, choose one useful item to donate to a person in need.
lessons.story: Imaan’s family is collecting warm clothes for families who need them. Imaan looks through her cupboard and chooses a good jacket that no longer fits. Ammi helps her fold it for the donation box.
lessons.question: Your family is collecting things for people in need. What could you do?

answers.text: Give something broken and useless.
answers.feedback: Giving is about caring. What could really help someone?

answers.text: Say it is not your job.
answers.feedback: Children can care for others too. Try again.

answers.text: With an adult, choose a useful item to give.
answers.feedback: That is a safe and caring way to help people in need.

lessons.title: Choose Good Company
lessons.arabic: مَثَلُ الْجَلِيسِ الصَّالِحِ وَالسَّوْءِ كَحَامِلِ الْمِسْكِ وَنَافِخِ الْكِيرِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Good friends influence us, just as sweet perfume spreads its scent.
lessons.explanation: Friends affect the choices we make. Look for companions who encourage you to be honest, caring and responsible.
lessons.action: Spend time today with someone who encourages a good habit.
lessons.story: Akhlaq has two friends. One always encourages him to finish his homework and tell the truth. The other often dares him to do silly, unsafe things. Akhlaq decides to spend more time with the friend who helps him be good.
lessons.question: Which friend would help you grow in good habits?

answers.text: A friend who encourages honesty and kindness.
answers.feedback: Good friends influence us for the better, like a sweet perfume.

answers.text: A friend who dares you to break rules.
answers.feedback: Friends affect our choices. Look for someone who helps you be good.

answers.text: Anyone, it does not matter.
answers.feedback: Our friends really do affect us. Think again.

lessons.title: Do Not Jump to Conclusions
lessons.arabic: إِيَّاكُمْ وَالظَّنَّ فَإِنَّ الظَّنَّ أَكْذَبُ الْحَدِيثِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Beware of harmful suspicion and unfounded assumptions.
lessons.explanation: A friend may seem quiet because they are tired, not because they are upset with you. Ask gently instead of guessing badly.
lessons.action: Before assuming someone meant harm, ask a calm, respectful question.
lessons.story: Imaan’s friend does not wave back at her in the morning. Imaan starts to think, “She must be angry with me.” Instead of guessing, she asks gently. Her friend says, “Sorry, I didn’t see you. I was so sleepy!”
lessons.question: A friend seems quiet today. What should you do?

answers.text: Decide they are angry with you.
answers.feedback: Guessing badly can be unfair. Is there a better way to find out?

answers.text: Tell others they are being rude.
answers.feedback: That spreads an unfair idea. Try a kinder choice.

answers.text: Ask them gently if everything is okay.
answers.feedback: Asking calmly is better than assuming the worst.

lessons.title: Keep Neighbors Safe
lessons.arabic: وَاللَّهِ لاَ يُؤْمِنُ ... الَّذِي لاَ يَأْمَنُ جَارُهُ بَوَائِقَهُ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: A neighbor should feel safe from our harm.
lessons.explanation: We can show respect to people living near us by being thoughtful, keeping noise down and caring for shared spaces.
lessons.action: Make one choice today that keeps your neighbors comfortable.
lessons.story: It is late in the evening, and Akhlaq wants to bounce his ball against the wall. He remembers the neighbour’s baby sleeps next door. He puts the ball away and plays a quiet game instead.
lessons.question: Your neighbour’s baby is sleeping. What could you do?

answers.text: Play loudly because it is your house.
answers.feedback: Neighbours should feel safe and comfortable near us. Try again.

answers.text: Choose a quiet activity.
answers.feedback: That keeps your neighbours comfortable. Thoughtful choice!

answers.text: Bang on the wall for fun.
answers.feedback: That could upset your neighbours. What would be considerate?

lessons.title: No Jealousy or Hate
lessons.arabic: لاَ تَبَاغَضُوا وَلاَ تَحَاسَدُوا وَلاَ تَدَابَرُوا
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Do not hate, envy or turn away from each other.
lessons.explanation: A friend’s success does not take away your chances. Cheer for others and keep your own heart peaceful.
lessons.action: Congratulate someone today on something they did well.
lessons.story: Imaan’s friend wins the drawing competition. For a moment, Imaan feels a little jealous. Then she walks over and says, “Mabrook! Your picture is beautiful.” Her heart feels lighter.
lessons.question: A friend wins something you wanted. What is the peaceful choice?

answers.text: Congratulate them sincerely.
answers.feedback: Cheering for others keeps your heart peaceful and your friendship strong.

answers.text: Say their work was not that good.
answers.feedback: That can hurt them and your own heart. Try again.

answers.text: Stop talking to them.
answers.feedback: Turning away from friends can damage friendship. Try a kinder choice.

lessons.title: No Cheating
lessons.arabic: مَنْ غَشَّ فَلَيْسَ مِنِّي
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Cheating is against the Prophet’s teaching.
lessons.explanation: Real achievement comes from your own effort. Being honest in a test, game or sale is more important than appearing to win.
lessons.action: In your next game or school task, follow the rules even when nobody is watching.
lessons.story: During a spelling test, Akhlaq could easily see his neighbour’s paper. Nobody is watching. He covers his eyes with his hand, takes a breath, and writes his own answers.
lessons.question: You could copy someone’s answers without anyone noticing. What is the honest choice?

answers.text: Copy just one answer.
answers.feedback: Even one copied answer is cheating. Try again.

answers.text: Do your own work honestly.
answers.feedback: Real achievement comes from your own effort. Well done!

answers.text: Ask your friend to show you all the answers.
answers.feedback: That is still cheating, even if they agree. Think again.

lessons.title: Keep Learning the Deen
lessons.arabic: مَنْ يُرِدِ اللَّهُ بِهِ خَيْرًا يُفَقِّهْهُ فِي الدِّينِ
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: Allah grants understanding of religion to someone He wishes good for.
lessons.explanation: Asking thoughtful questions and learning patiently are wonderful habits. There is always more good to discover.
lessons.action: Ask a teacher or parent one sincere question about Islam today.
lessons.story: Imaan wonders why Muslims fast in Ramadan. Instead of keeping the question to herself, she asks her teacher after class. Her teacher is happy to explain, and Imaan learns something new.
lessons.question: You have a question about Islam. What could you do?

answers.text: Keep it to yourself and stay confused.
answers.feedback: Asking is a wonderful way to learn. What could you do?

answers.text: Make up your own answer.
answers.feedback: It is better to learn from someone who knows. Try again.

answers.text: Ask a teacher or parent sincerely.
answers.feedback: Asking thoughtful questions is a beautiful habit of a learner.

lessons.title: Learn and Share Qur’an
lessons.arabic: خَيْرُكُمْ مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ الْقُرْآنَ وَعَلَّمَهُ
lessons.label: SHORT COMPLETE STATEMENT
lessons.meaning: Among the best are those who learn the Qur’an and teach it.
lessons.explanation: Every surah you learn is precious. You can share what you have learned in a gentle and encouraging way.
lessons.action: Revise one short surah and recite it to a trusted family member.
lessons.story: Akhlaq has just memorised Surah Al-Kawthar. His little sister is learning to read. He sits beside her and gently helps her with the first ayah, smiling when she gets it right.
lessons.question: You have learned a short surah. What could you do with it?

answers.text: Share it kindly with someone in your family.
answers.feedback: Learning and gently sharing the Qur’an is a precious thing.

answers.text: Laugh at people who do not know it.
answers.feedback: Laughing can discourage others. Try sharing it gently.

answers.text: Never recite it again.
answers.feedback: Practising helps it stay in your heart. Try again.

lessons.title: Begin with a Good Intention
lessons.arabic: إِنَّمَا الأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Actions are judged by intentions.
lessons.explanation: The reason behind your action matters. Before helping, studying or giving, quietly intend to please Allah.
lessons.action: Before your next good deed, make a sincere intention for Allah.
lessons.story: Imaan is about to help her teacher tidy the classroom. Before starting, she quietly thinks, “I’m doing this to please Allah.” Then she gets to work with a happy heart.
lessons.question: Before doing a good deed, what can you do?

answers.text: Make a sincere intention for Allah.
answers.feedback: The reason behind your action matters. A sincere intention is beautiful.

answers.text: Think only about who will praise you.
answers.feedback: Wanting praise can creep in. What intention could you make instead?

answers.text: Nothing, intentions do not matter.
answers.feedback: Intentions do matter. Try again.

lessons.title: Make Du’a in Sujud
lessons.arabic: أَقْرَبُ مَا يَكُونُ الْعَبْدُ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَهُوَ سَاجِدٌ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: A servant is especially close to Allah during prostration.
lessons.explanation: Sujud is a beautiful moment of worship. You can ask Allah for goodness while following the etiquette of prayer.
lessons.action: In your next appropriate sujud, make a short du’a in the way you have been taught.
lessons.story: Akhlaq is praying Maghrib with his family. In sujud, he remembers his teacher saying it is a special time to ask Allah for good. In his heart he asks Allah to help his grandmother feel better.
lessons.question: What is a beautiful thing to do in sujud, in the way you have been taught?

answers.text: Rush through it as fast as you can.
answers.feedback: Sujud is a special moment. Try a calmer choice.

answers.text: Make a short du’a in the way you have been taught.
answers.feedback: Sujud is a beautiful moment to ask Allah for goodness.

answers.text: Look around at what others are doing.
answers.feedback: Prayer is a time to focus on Allah. Try again.

lessons.title: Give Sincere Advice
lessons.arabic: الدِّينُ النَّصِيحَةُ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM A LONGER REPORT
lessons.meaning: Religion includes sincere care and good counsel.
lessons.explanation: Helping someone is not about embarrassing them. A good friend gives gentle advice and wants what is best for others.
lessons.action: If a friend needs help, offer one kind, private suggestion today.
lessons.story: Imaan notices her friend has her shoelace untied, and it might make her trip. Instead of shouting it in front of everyone, Imaan quietly tells her, “Your lace is loose, be careful.”
lessons.question: Your friend has made a small mistake. How could you help?

answers.text: Announce it loudly to the class.
answers.feedback: That might embarrass them. Is there a kinder way?

answers.text: Say nothing even if they might get hurt.
answers.feedback: Caring friends help each other. Try again.

answers.text: Give a kind, private suggestion.
answers.feedback: Gentle, private advice shows you want what is best for them.

lessons.title: Be the First to Make Peace
lessons.arabic: وَخَيْرُهُمَا الَّذِي يَبْدَأُ بِالسَّلَامِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: The better of two people who have fallen out is the one who begins with Salam.
lessons.explanation: Friendships sometimes have difficult days. Courage can mean taking the first peaceful step instead of waiting for the other person.
lessons.action: After a small disagreement, calmly greet the other person and offer to make peace.
lessons.story: Imaan and Akhlaq argued about whose turn it was on the swing. Now they are not speaking. Imaan feels nervous, but she walks over first and says, “Assalamu Alaikum. Shall we make up?” Akhlaq smiles with relief.
lessons.question: You and a friend had a small disagreement. What shows courage?

answers.text: Wait for them to say sorry first.
answers.feedback: Waiting can make the gap grow. Who could take the first step?

answers.text: Be the first to greet them and make peace.
answers.feedback: Taking the first peaceful step is real courage.

answers.text: Tell everyone how unfair they were.
answers.feedback: That can make things worse. Try a peaceful choice.

lessons.title: Never Use Insults
lessons.arabic: سِبَابُ الْمُسْلِمِ فُسُوقٌ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Insulting a Muslim is sinful behavior.
lessons.explanation: Strong people do not need hurtful names or insults to be heard. Even when you disagree, you can stay respectful.
lessons.action: Spend today speaking without calling anyone an insulting name.
lessons.story: During football, a boy calls Akhlaq a mean name. Akhlaq feels like calling him a worse name back. Instead, he says firmly, “Please don’t call me that. Let’s just play.”
lessons.question: Someone calls you an unkind name. What is the respectful choice?

answers.text: Call them a worse name back.
answers.feedback: Insults do not make you stronger. Try another way.

answers.text: Calmly ask them to stop, without insulting them.
answers.feedback: You stayed respectful even when you disagreed. That is strength.

answers.text: Make up a rude song about them.
answers.feedback: That is still insulting. Think of a respectful reply.

lessons.title: Do Not Carry Gossip
lessons.arabic: لَا يَدْخُلُ الْجَنَّةَ نَمَّامٌ
lessons.label: SHORT NARRATION
lessons.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ gave a serious warning against carrying harmful gossip between people.
lessons.explanation: Passing a hurtful message from one friend to another can break trust. You can be the person who stops the chain.
lessons.action: If someone shares gossip, do not pass it on; change to a kinder subject.
lessons.story: A girl at lunch whispers to Imaan, “Did you hear what Sana said about Hiba?” Imaan does not want to pass hurtful words around. She says, “Let’s talk about something else. Did you see the new library books?”
lessons.question: Someone tells you a hurtful piece of gossip. What could you do?

answers.text: Pass it on to another friend.
answers.feedback: Passing it on can break trust and hurt people. Try again.

answers.text: Add some extra details.
answers.feedback: That makes the hurt worse. What could stop the chain?

answers.text: Do not pass it on and change to a kinder subject.
answers.feedback: You stopped the chain. That protects friendships.

lessons.title: Check Before You Share
lessons.arabic: كَفَى بِالْمَرْءِ كَذِبًا أَنْ يُحَدِّثَ بِكُلِّ مَا سَمِعَ
lessons.label: COMPLETE CORE WORDING
lessons.meaning: Repeating everything you hear can make you spread falsehood.
lessons.explanation: Not every story or online message is true. Wise children stop, check, and ask a trusted adult before passing news along.
lessons.action: Before forwarding or repeating one story today, check whether it is true.
lessons.story: Akhlaq hears that school will be closed tomorrow. He is about to tell all his friends. Then he stops and asks his teacher first. It turns out the story was not true at all.
lessons.question: You hear some exciting news. What should you do before sharing it?

answers.text: Share it straight away with everyone.
answers.feedback: Not every story is true. What could you do first?

answers.text: Check with a trusted adult whether it is true.
answers.feedback: Checking first stops you from spreading something false. Wise choice!

answers.text: Make the story sound even bigger.
answers.feedback: That makes it less true. Try again.

lessons.title: Include Everyone
lessons.arabic: إِذَا كُنْتُمْ ثَلَاثَةً فَلَا يَتَنَاجَى رَجُلَانِ دُونَ الْآخَرِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: When three people are together, two should not whisper privately in a way that excludes the third.
lessons.explanation: Imagine how lonely a friend feels when everyone whispers without them. Your kindness can make the whole group feel welcome.
lessons.action: During a group activity, invite someone who seems left out into the conversation.
lessons.story: Imaan, Hiba and a new girl are working on a group project. Hiba starts whispering secrets to Imaan only. Imaan notices the new girl looking sad, so she says, “Let’s all decide together.”
lessons.question: In a group of three, two friends start whispering. What could you do?

answers.text: Bring everyone back into the conversation.
answers.feedback: Your kindness can make the whole group feel welcome.

answers.text: Whisper too and leave the third person out.
answers.feedback: Imagine how lonely that feels. Try again.

answers.text: Tell the third person to go away.
answers.feedback: That excludes them even more. What would be kinder?

lessons.title: Greet People You Meet
lessons.arabic: وَتَقْرَأُ السَّلَامَ عَلَى مَنْ عَرَفْتَ وَمَنْ لَمْ تَعْرِفْ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Offering Salam to people you know and those you do not know is among good Islamic manners.
lessons.explanation: A warm greeting makes a place friendlier. You do not need to be famous or important to spread peace.
lessons.action: Offer Salam politely to an appropriate person in your family or school today.
lessons.story: At the masjid, Akhlaq sees an elderly man he does not know. He remembers that salam is for everyone. He smiles and says, “Assalamu Alaikum,” and the man replies warmly.
lessons.question: You meet someone appropriate whom you do not know well, with your family nearby. What could you do?

answers.text: Ignore them because you do not know them.
answers.feedback: Salam can be for people you know and those you do not. Try again.

answers.text: Only greet your best friends.
answers.feedback: A greeting spreads peace to many people. Think again.

answers.text: Offer a polite salam.
answers.feedback: A warm greeting makes a place friendlier.

lessons.title: Ask Before Entering
lessons.arabic: إِذَا اسْتَأْذَنَ أَحَدُكُمْ ثَلَاثًا فَلَمْ يُؤْذَنْ لَهُ فَلْيَرْجِعْ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: If permission is not given after asking three times, leave instead of forcing entry.
lessons.explanation: Everyone needs personal space. Knocking and waiting shows that you respect other people's comfort and privacy.
lessons.action: Knock and wait for permission before entering a family member's room.
lessons.story: Imaan wants to borrow her brother’s colours. His door is closed. She knocks and waits. He says, “Not now, I’m changing.” Imaan says, “Okay!” and comes back later.
lessons.question: You want to go into a family member’s room. What is respectful?

answers.text: Burst in without knocking.
answers.feedback: Everyone needs personal space. What could you do first?

answers.text: Knock and wait for permission.
answers.feedback: Knocking and waiting shows you respect others’ privacy.

answers.text: Keep banging until they open.
answers.feedback: If they do not give permission, it is better to come back later.

lessons.title: Remember Allah at the Door
lessons.arabic: إِذَا دَخَلَ الرَّجُلُ بَيْتَهُ فَذَكَرَ اللَّهَ عِنْدَ دُخُولِهِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Remembering Allah when entering home is taught in the Sunnah.
lessons.explanation: Your home is a wonderful place to begin a good habit. Let your arrival be peaceful and full of remembrance.
lessons.action: When you come home today, say Bismillah and greet your family.
lessons.story: Akhlaq rushes home after school, shouting for his snack. Then he remembers. He steps in calmly, says Bismillah, and greets his family with salam. The house feels peaceful.
lessons.question: You are arriving home. What is a lovely way to come in?

answers.text: Say Bismillah and greet your family.
answers.feedback: Remembering Allah at the door makes your arrival peaceful.

answers.text: Slam the door and run to your room.
answers.feedback: That can startle your family. Try a calmer way.

answers.text: Shout for food straight away.
answers.feedback: There is a more peaceful way to arrive. Try again.

lessons.title: Show Good Manners in Shared Spaces
lessons.arabic: غَضُّ الْبَصَرِ وَكَفُّ الْأَذَى وَرَدُّ السَّلَامِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Good conduct in public places includes restraint, not causing harm, and returning greetings.
lessons.explanation: The street, school corridor, and park belong to many people. Every small respectful choice helps everyone feel comfortable.
lessons.action: In one shared space today, walk considerately and let someone pass without pushing.
lessons.story: The school corridor is crowded at break time. Imaan wants to get to the playground fast, but she walks calmly, lets a younger child pass, and returns a friend’s salam on the way.
lessons.question: A shared corridor is crowded. What shows good manners?

answers.text: Push through to get there first.
answers.feedback: Pushing can hurt others. Try a more considerate way.

answers.text: Run and shout through the crowd.
answers.feedback: Shared spaces belong to everyone. Try again.

answers.text: Walk considerately and let others pass.
answers.feedback: Small respectful choices help everyone feel comfortable.

lessons.title: Make Room for Someone
lessons.arabic: وَلَكِنْ تَفَسَّحُوا وَتَوَسَّعُوا
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Make space for others rather than pushing someone out of their seat.
lessons.explanation: You can make people feel welcome without saying a word. Sometimes simply moving over is a beautiful act of kindness.
lessons.action: Make room for someone to sit comfortably beside you today.
lessons.story: In circle time, a new boy has nowhere to sit. Akhlaq shuffles over and pats the space beside him. The boy sits down and smiles. Nobody had to say a word.
lessons.question: Someone has nowhere to sit. What could you do?

answers.text: Move over and make room for them.
answers.feedback: Simply moving over can be a beautiful act of kindness.

answers.text: Spread out so there is no space.
answers.feedback: That keeps them out. Think again.

answers.text: Tell them to sit on the floor far away.
answers.feedback: That can feel unwelcoming. Try a kinder choice.

lessons.title: Treasure Your Time
lessons.arabic: نِعْمَتَانِ مَغْبُونٌ فِيهِمَا كَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ الصِّحَّةُ وَالْفَرَاغُ
lessons.label: COMPLETE CORE WORDING
lessons.meaning: Health and free time are two blessings many people fail to use well.
lessons.explanation: Your minutes are special. You can play, rest, learn, and help others when you choose your time wisely.
lessons.action: Use ten minutes of free time for one useful activity you choose.
lessons.story: Imaan has a free afternoon. She could spend all of it on cartoons. She decides to watch one, then spends ten minutes reading a new book and helping Ammi water the plants.
lessons.question: You have some free time. What is a wise way to use part of it?

answers.text: Spend all of it doing nothing useful.
answers.feedback: Free time is a blessing. How could you use some of it well?

answers.text: Choose ten minutes for something useful.
answers.feedback: Your minutes are special. You chose your time wisely.

answers.text: Complain that you are bored.
answers.feedback: There are many useful things to choose from. Try again.

lessons.title: Make Learning Welcoming
lessons.arabic: يَسِّرُوا وَلَا تُعَسِّرُوا وَبَشِّرُوا وَلَا تُنَفِّرُوا
lessons.label: COMPLETE WORDING
lessons.meaning: Make things easier and encouraging rather than unnecessarily difficult or off-putting.
lessons.explanation: A good learner can also be a helpful teacher. Encourage others instead of making them feel silly for not knowing.
lessons.action: Explain one small lesson to someone patiently, without teasing them for a mistake.
lessons.story: Akhlaq’s younger cousin is learning to read Urdu and gets a word wrong. Akhlaq’s friend laughs. Akhlaq says, “That’s okay! It’s tricky. Let’s try it together.”
lessons.question: Someone makes a mistake while learning. How could you help?

answers.text: Laugh at the mistake.
answers.feedback: Laughing can make learning feel scary. Try again.

answers.text: Explain kindly and encourage them.
answers.feedback: Making learning easy and encouraging is a beautiful way to help.

answers.text: Tell them they will never learn.
answers.feedback: That can stop them from trying. Think of an encouraging choice.

lessons.title: Return What You Borrow
lessons.arabic: إِنَّ خِيَارَكُمْ أَحْسَنُكُمْ قَضَاءً
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: The best people fulfill what they owe generously and well.
lessons.explanation: Borrowed pencils, books, and toys are a trust. Returning them carefully shows people they can rely on you.
lessons.action: Return one borrowed item today in good condition, or remind yourself to return it on time.
lessons.story: Imaan borrowed her friend’s book last week. She has nearly forgotten about it. When she finds it on her shelf, she makes sure it is clean, puts it in her bag, and returns it the next morning with a thank-you note.
lessons.question: You borrowed something from a friend. What should you do?

answers.text: Keep it because they might forget.
answers.feedback: Borrowed things are a trust. Try again.

answers.text: Return it late and damaged.
answers.feedback: Others rely on you to care for their things. Think again.

answers.text: Return it on time and in good condition.
answers.feedback: People can rely on you. That is a beautiful habit.

lessons.title: Work Toward What Benefits You
lessons.arabic: احْرِصْ عَلَى مَا يَنْفَعُكَ وَاسْتَعِنْ بِاللَّهِ وَلَا تَعْجِزْ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Work for what benefits you, seek Allah's help, and do not give up helplessly.
lessons.explanation: A difficult homework question or skill is not the end of the journey. Do your best, ask Allah for help, and try again.
lessons.action: Choose one difficult but helpful task and work on it for ten focused minutes.
lessons.story: Akhlaq is learning to ride a bicycle and keeps wobbling. He feels like giving up. He makes a du’a for help, gets back on, and practises for ten more minutes. Slowly, it gets easier.
lessons.question: Something helpful is hard to learn. What could you do?

answers.text: Give up straight away.
answers.feedback: Difficult is not the end of the journey. Try again.

answers.text: Do your best, ask Allah for help and keep trying.
answers.feedback: Working hard and seeking Allah’s help is a strong way forward.

answers.text: Blame others for it being hard.
answers.feedback: Blaming does not help us learn. What could you do?

lessons.title: Ask Allah with Hope
lessons.arabic: إِذَا دَعَا أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَعْزِمِ الْمَسْأَلَةَ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: When making Du'a, ask Allah sincerely and with conviction.
lessons.explanation: Your Du'a matters. Ask with hope, knowing Allah is wise and responds as He wills.
lessons.action: Make one sincere Du'a for something good, using your own respectful words.
lessons.story: Imaan’s grandmother is in hospital. Imaan raises her hands and makes a sincere du’a in her own words, asking Allah to make her grandmother well. She asks with hope, trusting that Allah is wise.
lessons.question: You want to ask Allah for something good. How could you make du’a?

answers.text: Ask sincerely and with hope.
answers.feedback: Your du’a matters. Asking with hope is beautiful.

answers.text: Say it quickly without thinking.
answers.feedback: Du’a is a special conversation with Allah. Try again.

answers.text: Think there is no point asking.
answers.feedback: Allah hears every du’a. Try a more hopeful choice.

lessons.title: Honor Prayer Time
lessons.arabic: الصَّلَاةُ عَلَى وَقْتِهَا
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Prayer at its proper time is among the deeds especially loved by Allah.
lessons.explanation: Prayer is a special meeting with Allah. Learning to prepare for it is a beautiful step, at your own age and ability.
lessons.action: When the next prayer time arrives, help prepare a prayer space or pray with guidance.
lessons.story: The adhan sounds for Asr. Akhlaq is in the middle of a game. He pauses, helps Baba lay out the prayer mats, and joins the family prayer with guidance.
lessons.question: You hear that it is prayer time. What could you do?

answers.text: Keep playing and forget about it.
answers.feedback: Prayer time is a special meeting with Allah. What could you do?

answers.text: Help prepare a prayer space or pray with guidance.
answers.feedback: Preparing for prayer is a beautiful step, at your age and ability.

answers.text: Complain that it always interrupts you.
answers.feedback: It is okay to feel that way sometimes. How could you respond kindly?

lessons.title: Prayer Helps Us Begin Again
lessons.arabic: فَذَلِكَ مِثْلُ الصَّلَوَاتِ الْخَمْسِ يَمْحُو اللَّهُ بِهَا الْخَطَايَا
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: The five daily prayers are compared to repeated washing that removes dirt.
lessons.explanation: Just as washing makes us physically clean, Salah brings us back to Allah and helps us seek forgiveness and improvement.
lessons.action: After a prayer today, ask Allah to help you improve one habit.
lessons.story: Imaan was unkind to her brother today and feels bad. After praying, she asks Allah to help her be more patient tomorrow. She also says sorry to her brother.
lessons.question: You made a mistake today. What could you do after prayer?

answers.text: Ask Allah to help you improve.
answers.feedback: Salah helps us come back to Allah and seek improvement.

answers.text: Decide you can never change.
answers.feedback: Everyone can improve. Try a more hopeful choice.

answers.text: Pretend it never happened.
answers.feedback: Being honest with ourselves helps us grow. Try again.

lessons.title: Two Beautiful Phrases
lessons.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ الْعَظِيمِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: These two short phrases are beloved to the Most Merciful and weighty in reward.
lessons.explanation: Even a short phrase can fill your day with remembrance. Learn it gently and say it with attention.
lessons.action: Recite these two phrases after learning their meaning with a parent or teacher.
lessons.story: Akhlaq is waiting in the car for Ammi. Instead of feeling bored, he quietly practises the two phrases his teacher taught him, thinking about their meaning as he says them.
lessons.question: You are waiting with nothing to do. What could fill the moment?

answers.text: Quietly remember Allah with phrases you have learned.
answers.feedback: Even a short phrase can fill your day with remembrance.

answers.text: Complain about waiting.
answers.feedback: Waiting can be a chance to remember Allah. Try again.

answers.text: Kick the seat in front.
answers.feedback: That can disturb others. What could you do instead?

lessons.title: Four Words of Dhikr
lessons.arabic: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Four phrases of remembrance are especially beloved to Allah.
lessons.explanation: These words praise Allah and remind us of His greatness. You can carry them in your heart wherever you go.
lessons.action: Learn and recite all four phrases today, one at a time.
lessons.story: Imaan and Ammi go for a walk and see a beautiful sunset. Imaan wants to say something to praise Allah. Ammi teaches her four phrases of remembrance, one at a time, and Imaan says each one slowly.
lessons.question: You see something beautiful in nature. What could you do?

answers.text: Say nothing and forget it.
answers.feedback: Beautiful moments can remind us of Allah. Try again.

answers.text: Remember and praise Allah.
answers.feedback: Praising Allah when we see His creation is a lovely habit.

answers.text: Take a photo and boast about it.
answers.feedback: Enjoying it is fine, but what could your heart remember?

lessons.title: Send Salawat
lessons.arabic: مَنْ صَلَّى عَلَيَّ وَاحِدَةً صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ عَشْرًا
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Whoever sends one blessing upon the Prophet ﷺ receives ten blessings from Allah.
lessons.explanation: Sending Salawat reminds us of our love and respect for the Prophet ﷺ, whose example helps us become better.
lessons.action: Recite one complete Salawat today with attention and respect.
lessons.story: In class, the teacher mentions the Prophet ﷺ. Akhlaq quietly sends salawat with love and respect. After school, Dadi Jaan helps him learn a complete salawat to recite with attention.
lessons.question: When you hear the name of the Prophet ﷺ, what could you do?

answers.text: Send salawat with respect.
answers.feedback: Sending salawat shows love and respect for the Prophet ﷺ.

answers.text: Ignore it.
answers.feedback: His example helps us become better. How could you show respect?

answers.text: Make a joke.
answers.feedback: His name deserves respect. Try again.

lessons.title: Keep Trying to Recite
lessons.arabic: وَالَّذِي يَقْرَأُ الْقُرْآنَ وَيَتَتَعْتَعُ فِيهِ وَهُوَ عَلَيْهِ شَاقٌّ لَهُ أَجْرَانِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: A person who recites the Qur'an with difficulty while striving has two rewards.
lessons.explanation: Do not feel embarrassed when a verse seems hard. Allah knows your effort, and patient practice is precious.
lessons.action: Practise one difficult Qur'anic verse slowly with a teacher or trusted recitation audio.
lessons.story: Imaan finds a new ayah very hard to read. She stumbles on the words and feels embarrassed. Her teacher smiles and says, “Keep going slowly.” Imaan practises again, one word at a time.
lessons.question: A verse of the Qur’an is hard for you to read. What could you do?

answers.text: Give up because it is too difficult.
answers.feedback: Allah knows your effort. Patient practice is precious.

answers.text: Practise slowly with a teacher.
answers.feedback: Striving with patience is beautiful. Keep going!

answers.text: Feel ashamed and hide it.
answers.feedback: There is no need to feel embarrassed. Try a braver choice.

lessons.title: Make Time for Qur'an
lessons.arabic: اقْرَءُوا الْقُرْآنَ فَإِنَّهُ يَأْتِي يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ شَفِيعًا لِأَصْحَابِهِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Recite the Qur'an; it will intercede for those devoted to it on the Day of Resurrection.
lessons.explanation: The Qur'an is not a race. A small daily connection, made with respect, can grow into a lifelong friendship with Allah's Book.
lessons.action: Spend five focused minutes reciting or listening attentively to Qur'an today.
lessons.story: Akhlaq’s evenings are full of homework and play. He decides to keep five special minutes each day for the Qur’an. Some days he recites, other days he listens carefully with Baba.
lessons.question: How could you build a friendship with the Qur’an?

answers.text: Only open it once a year.
answers.feedback: A small daily connection can grow into a lifelong friendship.

answers.text: Rush through as much as possible without care.
answers.feedback: The Qur’an is not a race. Try again.

answers.text: Spend a few focused minutes with it each day.
answers.feedback: A small daily connection, made with respect, is wonderful.

lessons.title: Every Letter Matters
lessons.arabic: مَنْ قَرَأَ حَرْفًا مِنْ كِتَابِ اللَّهِ فَلَهُ بِهِ حَسَنَةٌ
lessons.label: EXCERPT; HASAN GRADING (DARUSSALAM); TIRMIDHI: HASAN SAHIH
lessons.meaning: Reciting even a letter from Allah's Book brings reward, as described in this Hadith.
lessons.explanation: Small steps are worth taking. Keep reciting correctly, even if you are learning just a little today.
lessons.action: Recite a short passage with care and correct your pronunciation with a qualified guide.
lessons.story: Imaan is learning only a few new letters each day in her Qaida. Sometimes she feels slow. Her teacher reminds her that every small step matters. Imaan practises carefully and asks for corrections.
lessons.question: You can only learn a little Qur’an today. What should you remember?

answers.text: Small steps are still worth taking.
answers.feedback: Keep reciting correctly, even if just a little today.

answers.text: It is not worth trying if it is only a little.
answers.feedback: Every small step matters. Try again.

answers.text: Rush so you can finish faster.
answers.feedback: Careful recitation is better than rushing. Think again.

lessons.title: Discover Surah Al-Ikhlas
lessons.arabic: إِنَّهَا لَتَعْدِلُ ثُلُثَ الْقُرْآنِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ taught the great virtue of Surah Al-Ikhlas, describing it as equivalent to one-third of the Qur'an.
lessons.explanation: This small surah teaches the oneness of Allah. Its short length makes it a wonderful place to strengthen correct recitation and understanding.
