lessons.action: Recite Surah Al-Ikhlas slowly today and explain one idea about Allah's oneness.
lessons.story: Akhlaq learns Surah Al-Ikhlas in class. At dinner, he recites it slowly for his family and explains one thing: “It teaches that Allah is One.” Baba nods proudly.
lessons.question: What does Surah Al-Ikhlas teach us about?

answers.text: The oneness of Allah.
answers.feedback: That is right! This short surah teaches the oneness of Allah.

answers.text: How to play a game.
answers.feedback: Not quite. Think about what the surah says about Allah.

answers.text: The weather.
answers.feedback: Try again. What does the surah teach about Allah?

lessons.title: Review What You Memorize
lessons.arabic: تَعَاهَدُوا الْقُرْآنَ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Keep revising and taking care of the Qur'an you have learned.
lessons.explanation: Memorization is like caring for a beautiful garden. Revising an old surah helps it stay fresh in your heart.
lessons.action: Revise one surah you already know without looking, then check any mistakes.
lessons.story: Imaan learned Surah An-Nas last year, but she has not recited it for a while. She tries it from memory and stumbles on one ayah. She checks it carefully, practises again, and it feels fresh in her heart.
lessons.question: You memorised a surah a long time ago. What should you do?

answers.text: Never think about it again.
answers.feedback: Memorisation needs care, like a garden. Try again.

answers.text: Revise it regularly and check mistakes.
answers.feedback: Revising helps it stay fresh in your heart.

answers.text: Pretend you still know it perfectly.
answers.feedback: Being honest helps you improve. What could you do?

lessons.title: Respect Older and Younger
lessons.arabic: لَيْسَ مِنَّا مَنْ لَمْ يَرْحَمْ صَغِيرَنَا وَيَعْرِفْ شَرَفَ كَبِيرِنَا
lessons.label: EXCERPT; HASAN GRADING (DARUSSALAM)
lessons.meaning: Show kindness to younger children and proper respect to older people.
lessons.explanation: Everyone deserves dignity. You can be gentle with little children and considerate toward elders.
lessons.action: Offer respectful help to an older family member or kindness to a younger child today.
lessons.story: At a family gathering, Akhlaq helps his little cousin reach the juice. Then he gives his chair to Nana Abbu, who has just arrived. Both of them smile at him.
lessons.question: At a family gathering, what shows respect for young and old?

answers.text: Ignore the little ones and the elders.
answers.feedback: Everyone deserves dignity. Try again.

answers.text: Be gentle with younger children and respectful to elders.
answers.feedback: That is a beautiful way to honour everyone in the family.

answers.text: Only care about your own friends.
answers.feedback: Family includes young and old. Think again.

lessons.title: Be Patient with People
lessons.arabic: خَدَمْتُ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَشْرَ سِنِينَ فَمَا قَالَ لِي أُفٍّ
lessons.label: NARRATOR'S REPORT; EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Anas رضي الله عنه reported that the Prophet ﷺ treated him with remarkable patience during years of service.
lessons.explanation: People are still learning, and mistakes happen. The Prophet's gentleness is an example for the way we speak at home.
lessons.action: When someone makes a small mistake, respond without saying 'ugh' or scolding them.
lessons.story: Imaan’s little brother spills paint on her drawing by accident. She wants to say “Ugh!” but she stops. She takes a breath and says, “It’s okay. Let’s clean it up together.”
lessons.question: Someone makes a small mistake that annoys you. What is a patient response?

answers.text: Say “Ugh!” and scold them.
answers.feedback: Mistakes happen, and people are still learning. Try a gentler way.

answers.text: Refuse to talk to them.
answers.feedback: Silence can hurt too. How could you respond gently?

answers.text: Respond calmly without scolding.
answers.feedback: Gentle patience is a beautiful example to follow at home.

lessons.title: Visit Someone Who Is Unwell
lessons.arabic: وَعِيَادَةُ الْمَرِيضِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Visiting the sick is among the rights Muslims owe one another.
lessons.explanation: When someone is ill, a gentle check-in can brighten the day. Always follow family and health guidance for visits.
lessons.action: With a parent's help, send a kind message or Du'a to someone who is unwell.
lessons.story: Akhlaq’s friend is ill and has missed school all week. Akhlaq asks Ammi to help him send a kind voice message: “Get well soon! I made du’a for you.” His friend feels cheered up.
lessons.question: A friend is unwell at home. What could you do?

answers.text: With a parent’s help, send a kind message or du’a.
answers.feedback: A gentle check-in can brighten someone’s day.

answers.text: Forget about them until they return.
answers.feedback: Your care could make them feel better. Try again.

answers.text: Visit without asking your family first.
answers.feedback: Always follow family and health guidance. What could you do safely?

lessons.title: Receive Gifts Gratefully
lessons.arabic: كَانَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يَقْبَلُ الْهَدِيَّةَ وَيُثِيبُ عَلَيْهَا
lessons.label: NARRATOR'S REPORT
lessons.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ accepted gifts and would respond with a return gift.
lessons.explanation: A gift is not about its price. A grateful heart notices the love, care, and effort behind it.
lessons.action: Thank someone sincerely for something they gave or did for you.
lessons.story: Imaan’s little cousin gives her a drawing of a flower. It is a bit scribbly. Imaan says, “Thank you! I love it,” and puts it on her wall. Then she makes a small card for her cousin in return.
lessons.question: Someone gives you a small gift. How could you respond?

answers.text: Say it is not good enough.
answers.feedback: A gift is about the love behind it. Try again.

answers.text: Thank them sincerely.
answers.feedback: A grateful heart notices the care behind a gift.

answers.text: Throw it away in front of them.
answers.feedback: That would hurt their feelings. Think again.

lessons.title: Children Deserve Greetings Too
lessons.arabic: أَنَّهُ مَرَّ عَلَى صِبْيَانٍ فَسَلَّمَ عَلَيْهِمْ
lessons.label: NARRATOR'S REPORT; EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Anas رضي الله عنه greeted children and said the Prophet ﷺ used to do so.
lessons.explanation: Every child matters. A greeting says: 'I see you, and you belong here.'
lessons.action: Offer a kind Salam to a younger sibling or child today.
lessons.story: Akhlaq walks past a group of younger children playing in the park. He smiles and says, “Assalamu Alaikum!” The little ones wave back happily, feeling noticed.
lessons.question: You pass by some younger children. What could you do?

answers.text: Walk past as if they are not there.
answers.feedback: Every child matters. How could you show that?

answers.text: Offer them a kind salam.
answers.feedback: A greeting says “I see you, and you belong here.”

answers.text: Tell them to move out of your way.
answers.feedback: That can feel unkind. Try a friendlier choice.

lessons.title: Plant Something Good
lessons.arabic: مَا مِنْ مُسْلِمٍ يَغْرِسُ غَرْسًا أَوْ يَزْرَعُ زَرْعًا
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Planting something that others benefit from is rewarded as charity.
lessons.explanation: A small plant can give shade, beauty, and food. Caring for the earth is one way to do lasting good.
lessons.action: Plant a seed or help water a family plant responsibly today.
lessons.story: Imaan plants a small tomato seed in a pot with Nani. Every day, she waters it carefully. Weeks later, the plant grows, and the whole family enjoys the tomatoes.
lessons.question: How could you do lasting good for the world around you?

answers.text: Plant a seed or care for a plant.
answers.feedback: A small plant can give shade, beauty and food. Lovely choice!

answers.text: Pull up plants for fun.
answers.feedback: Plants are part of Allah’s creation. Try again.

answers.text: Leave rubbish in the garden.
answers.feedback: That harms the earth. What could you do instead?

lessons.title: Never Hurt Animals for Fun
lessons.arabic: نَهَى رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنْ يُتَّخَذَ شَيْءٌ فِيهِ الرُّوحُ غَرَضًا
lessons.label: NARRATOR'S REPORT; SAHIH GRADING (DARUSSALAM)
lessons.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ prohibited using living creatures as targets for entertainment.
lessons.explanation: Animals are living beings, not toys to frighten or hurt. Being gentle includes leaving creatures safe.
lessons.action: Keep an animal safe today: observe it gently without chasing, throwing things, or disturbing it.
lessons.story: At the park, some boys throw stones at a stray cat to make it run. Akhlaq says, “Stop, that could hurt it!” He tells a nearby adult, and they leave the cat in peace.
lessons.question: Some children are throwing things at an animal for fun. What could you do?

answers.text: Join in because it looks funny.
answers.feedback: Animals are living beings, not toys. Try again.

answers.text: Ask them to stop and tell an adult.
answers.feedback: Being gentle includes keeping creatures safe.

answers.text: Throw things too.
answers.feedback: That could hurt the animal. Think of a gentle choice.

chunks: أَنْ يُتَّخَذَ شَيْءٌ فِيهِ الرُّوحُ غَرَضًا

lessons.title: Protect Water from Filth
lessons.arabic: لَا يَبُولَنَّ أَحَدُكُمْ فِي الْمَاءِ الدَّائِمِ الَّذِي لَا يَجْرِي
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ forbade polluting still water in this way.
lessons.explanation: Clean water matters to people, animals, and our environment. We should never contaminate it.
lessons.action: Help protect water today by keeping trash and dirt away from a water source.
lessons.story: On a family picnic by a pond, Imaan sees an empty wrapper floating near the edge. With Baba’s help, she picks it out with a stick and puts all their rubbish in a bag to take home.
lessons.question: You are near a pond or stream. How could you protect the water?

answers.text: Throw your rubbish in it.
answers.feedback: Clean water matters to people and animals. Try again.

answers.text: Keep rubbish and dirt away from the water.
answers.feedback: You helped protect water for everyone. Well done!

answers.text: Pour dirty water into it.
answers.feedback: That contaminates the water. Think of a cleaner choice.

lessons.title: Cover and Protect Food
lessons.arabic: غَطُّوا الْإِنَاءَ وَأَوْكُوا السِّقَاءَ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Cover vessels and secure water containers, as taught in the Sunnah.
lessons.explanation: Simple habits help keep food and water protected. You can support your family with careful, tidy routines.
lessons.action: With adult guidance, cover one stored food item or water container properly.
lessons.story: After dinner, Akhlaq sees the leftover food and the water jug left open on the table. With Ammi’s guidance, he covers the dish and puts the lid on the jug.
lessons.question: Food or water is left uncovered. What could you do?

answers.text: Leave it open overnight.
answers.feedback: Simple habits keep food and water protected. Try again.

answers.text: With adult guidance, cover it properly.
answers.feedback: Careful, tidy routines help protect your family’s food.

answers.text: Put your fingers in it.
answers.feedback: That is not hygienic. What would protect it?

lessons.title: Pets Need Kind Care
lessons.arabic: فَلَمْ تُطْعِمْهَا وَلَمْ تَدَعْهَا تَأْكُلُ
lessons.label: EXCERPT FROM WARNING NARRATION; ADAPT SENSITIVELY FOR YOUNG CHILDREN
lessons.meaning: A serious warning is given in a narration about keeping a cat confined without food or freedom to find food.
lessons.explanation: If we care for an animal, we must also care for its needs. Love means responsibility, not just playing.
lessons.action: With a parent, make sure a pet or garden animal has suitable water and care.
lessons.story: Imaan’s family looks after a cat. One morning, Imaan wants to play straight away. She remembers that caring for a pet means looking after its needs, so she first checks with Ammi that the cat has fresh water and food.
lessons.question: You look after a pet. What does kind care include?

answers.text: Only playing with it when you want.
answers.feedback: Love means responsibility, not just playing. Try again.

answers.text: With a parent, making sure it has water and care.
answers.feedback: Caring for an animal includes its needs. That is real love.

answers.text: Forgetting about it for days.
answers.feedback: A pet depends on us. Think of a caring choice.

lessons.title: Give Before You Are Asked
lessons.arabic: أَنْ تَصَدَّقَ وَأَنْتَ صَحِيحٌ شَحِيحٌ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Giving charity willingly while healthy and attached to what one has is especially meaningful.
lessons.explanation: Generosity is not only about giving what you no longer want. Sometimes sharing something you value is the bigger step.
lessons.action: With your parent's permission, share a useful item or some of your savings for a good cause.
lessons.story: Akhlaq has been saving coins for a new toy. At the masjid, there is a collection for a family in need. With Baba’s permission, he puts in some of his savings, even though it is hard.
lessons.question: You have something you value. What shows real generosity?

answers.text: Only give things you do not want anymore.
answers.feedback: Generosity can mean sharing something you value. Try again.

answers.text: With permission, share some of what you value for a good cause.
answers.feedback: Sharing something you value is a bigger, beautiful step.

answers.text: Never share anything.
answers.feedback: Sharing can make someone’s life better. Think again.

lessons.title: Giving Does Not Reduce True Good
lessons.arabic: مَا نَقَصَتْ صَدَقَةٌ مِنْ مَالٍ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Charity does not decrease wealth in the way we may fear; the Hadith speaks of its blessing.
lessons.explanation: When you give sincerely, you are choosing kindness over keeping everything to yourself.
lessons.action: Put aside a small amount for charity, with a parent's help.
lessons.story: Imaan worries that if she gives some of her pocket money to charity, she will have less. Ammi helps her put aside a small amount. Imaan feels happy choosing kindness over keeping everything.
lessons.question: You are unsure about giving a little to charity. What could you do?

answers.text: With a parent’s help, set aside a small amount.
answers.feedback: When you give sincerely, you choose kindness.

answers.text: Keep it all and never give.
answers.feedback: Giving can bring blessing. Try again.

answers.text: Make fun of people who give.
answers.feedback: Giving is a beautiful choice. Think again.

lessons.title: Be Happy to Give
lessons.arabic: الْيَدُ الْعُلْيَا خَيْرٌ مِنَ الْيَدِ السُّفْلَى
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: The giving hand is better than the receiving hand, in the context of charity and self-reliance.
lessons.explanation: Giving is lovely, and needing help is never shameful. Start by sharing what you responsibly can.
lessons.action: Offer one useful thing or act of help without waiting to be asked.
lessons.story: Akhlaq sees his classmate has forgotten a pencil for the test. Without waiting to be asked, he offers his spare one. His classmate is grateful, and Akhlaq feels happy to give.
lessons.question: A classmate needs something you have spare. What could you do?

answers.text: Offer it without waiting to be asked.
answers.feedback: Giving happily is lovely. And needing help is never shameful.

answers.text: Hide your spare one.
answers.feedback: Sharing what you responsibly can is a good choice. Try again.

answers.text: Laugh because they forgot.
answers.feedback: Everyone forgets sometimes. Think of a kinder choice.

lessons.title: Respect Even a Tiny Gift
lessons.arabic: لَا تَحْقِرَنَّ جَارَةٌ لِجَارَتِهَا وَلَوْ فِرْسِنَ شَاةٍ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Do not look down on a small gift from a neighbor.
lessons.explanation: A small present may carry a huge amount of care. Your gratitude can make the giver feel valued.
lessons.action: Thank someone kindly for a small gift or gesture, without comparing its price.
lessons.story: The neighbour Aunty sends over a small plate of halwa. Imaan’s friend says, “That’s all?” Imaan says, “It was so kind of her!” and thanks Aunty warmly the next day.
lessons.question: A neighbour gives you a very small gift. How could you respond?

answers.text: Complain that it is too small.
answers.feedback: A small gift may carry a huge amount of care. Try again.

answers.text: Compare it to bigger gifts.
answers.feedback: Comparing can hurt the giver. Think again.

answers.text: Thank them kindly for their care.
answers.feedback: Your gratitude makes the giver feel valued.

lessons.title: Good Work Can Be Charity
lessons.arabic: يَعْمَلُ بِيَدِهِ فَيَنْفَعُ نَفْسَهُ وَيَتَصَدَّقُ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: Useful work can benefit a person and provide opportunities to give.
lessons.explanation: Doing a task well is a wonderful skill. Even small helpful work teaches care and responsibility.
lessons.action: Complete one useful household task thoroughly and without expecting a prize.
lessons.story: Akhlaq is asked to sweep the courtyard. He could do it quickly and leave the corners dusty. Instead, he sweeps every corner carefully. When he finishes, he feels proud of a job done well.
lessons.question: You are given a household task. How could you do it?

answers.text: Do it carelessly so you finish fast.
answers.feedback: Doing a task well is a wonderful skill. Try again.

answers.text: Complete it thoroughly without expecting a prize.
answers.feedback: That is care and responsibility. Well done!

answers.text: Refuse unless you get paid.
answers.feedback: Helpful work is good in itself. Think again.

lessons.title: Faith Is Not Meant to Overwhelm
lessons.arabic: إِنَّ الدِّينَ يُسْرٌ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: The religion is easy; we should not make worship excessively difficult.
lessons.explanation: Growing in faith takes patience. Start with what you can do correctly and keep learning step by step.
lessons.action: Choose one small act of worship you can practise calmly and consistently this week.
lessons.story: Imaan wants to do lots of extra worship all at once, but she gets tired and gives up. Her teacher suggests choosing one small act she can do calmly every day. Imaan chooses saying Bismillah before eating.
lessons.question: You want to grow in worship. What is a wise way to start?

answers.text: Try to do everything at once.
answers.feedback: Growing in faith takes patience. Try a steadier step.

answers.text: Choose one small act you can do calmly and regularly.
answers.feedback: Starting with what you can do well, and growing step by step, is wise.

answers.text: Give up because it feels too hard.
answers.feedback: Faith is not meant to overwhelm you. Try again.

lessons.title: Rest When You Truly Need Rest
lessons.arabic: إِذَا نَعَسَ أَحَدُكُمْ وَهُوَ يُصَلِّي فَلْيَرْقُدْ حَتَّى يَذْهَبَ عَنْهُ النَّوْمُ
lessons.label: EXCERPT; ADULT EXPLAINS PRAYER CONTEXT
lessons.meaning: Someone extremely sleepy during voluntary prayer should rest until the sleepiness passes.
lessons.explanation: Good learning needs a rested mind. Our body is an amanah, so sensible rest matters too.
lessons.action: Tonight, prepare for sleep on time rather than staying up unnecessarily.
lessons.story: Akhlaq wants to stay up very late to finish a cartoon series. He knows he has school tomorrow and feels very sleepy. He decides to switch off the screen and get ready for bed on time.
lessons.question: It is getting late and you are very sleepy. What is a sensible choice?

answers.text: Stay up as late as possible.
answers.feedback: A rested mind learns better. Try again.

answers.text: Get ready for sleep on time.
answers.feedback: Our body is an amanah. Sensible rest matters.

answers.text: Drink fizzy drinks to stay awake.
answers.feedback: That might make sleep harder. Think again.

lessons.title: Be Fair and Easy in Transactions
lessons.arabic: رَحِمَ اللَّهُ رَجُلًا سَمْحًا إِذَا بَاعَ وَإِذَا اشْتَرَى
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ prayed for mercy for someone who is gracious in buying and selling.
lessons.explanation: Whether you are exchanging stickers or buying supplies, you can be fair, calm, and considerate.
lessons.action: In one small exchange today, be honest, polite, and fair to the other person.
lessons.story: Imaan and her friend are swapping stickers. Imaan notices one of hers is torn. Instead of hiding it, she says, “This one is torn. Let me give you a different one.” Her friend appreciates her fairness.
lessons.question: You are swapping things with a friend. What is fair?

answers.text: Hide the damaged item and swap it anyway.
answers.feedback: Being fair means being honest. Try again.

answers.text: Be honest, polite and fair in the swap.
answers.feedback: Fair and considerate dealings make friendships stronger.

answers.text: Argue until you get the best deal.
answers.feedback: There is a calmer, fairer way. Think again.

lessons.title: Choose the Easier Good Option
lessons.arabic: مَا خُيِّرَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ بَيْنَ أَمْرَيْنِ إِلَّا أَخَذَ أَيْسَرَهُمَا مَا لَمْ يَكُنْ إِثْمًا
lessons.label: NARRATOR'S DESCRIPTION; EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: When choosing between permissible options, the Prophet ﷺ often chose the easier one.
lessons.explanation: Wise choices do not have to be complicated. Pick what is good, permissible, and manageable rather than making everything hard.
lessons.action: For one task today, choose a simple, honest way to finish it properly.
lessons.story: Akhlaq has a school project. He thinks of making it hugely complicated and stressful. Imaan suggests a simple, honest plan that he can finish properly. He chooses the easier good option and does it well.
lessons.question: You can choose between two good ways to do a task. What is wise?

answers.text: Choose the simple, honest way and finish properly.
answers.feedback: Wise choices do not have to be complicated.

answers.text: Always choose the hardest way, even if you cannot finish.
answers.feedback: Making everything hard is not needed. Try again.

answers.text: Choose a way that involves cheating because it is easier.
answers.feedback: Easy is only good when it is also honest. Think again.

lessons.title: Learn from a Mistake
lessons.arabic: لَا يُلْدَغُ الْمُؤْمِنُ مِنْ جُحْرٍ وَاحِدٍ مَرَّتَيْنِ
lessons.label: COMPLETE CORE WORDING
lessons.meaning: A believer should learn from harmful experiences rather than repeating the same avoidable mistake.
lessons.explanation: Mistakes can teach you something valuable. Being wise means noticing what happened and changing your next step.
lessons.action: Think of one recent mistake and choose one specific way to avoid repeating it.
lessons.story: Imaan left her homework until the last minute and felt stressed. The next week, she remembers how that felt. This time, she does a little each day and finishes calmly.
lessons.question: You made a mistake last time. What is a wise next step?

answers.text: Repeat the same mistake.
answers.feedback: Mistakes can teach us something valuable. Try again.

answers.text: Notice what happened and change your next step.
answers.feedback: Being wise means learning from what happened.

answers.text: Blame someone else.
answers.feedback: Blaming does not help you learn. Think again.

lessons.title: Start with the Right Shoe
lessons.arabic: إِذَا انْتَعَلَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَبْدَأْ بِالْيُمْنَى
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: When putting on shoes, begin with the right foot.
lessons.explanation: A small habit can remind you to follow the Sunnah in ordinary parts of your day.
lessons.action: Put on your right shoe first today, and take off the left shoe first.
lessons.story: Akhlaq is rushing to get ready for school. As he puts on his shoes, he pauses and remembers to start with the right shoe. When he gets home, he takes off the left one first.
lessons.question: You are putting on your shoes. Which one could you start with?

answers.text: The left shoe.
answers.feedback: Try again. Which foot does the Sunnah say to begin with?

answers.text: The right shoe.
answers.feedback: Yes! A small habit helps you follow the Sunnah every day.

answers.text: It does not matter at all.
answers.feedback: There is a Sunnah for this small moment. Think again.

lessons.title: Prefer the Right in Good Things
lessons.arabic: كَانَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ يُعْجِبُهُ التَّيَمُّنُ
lessons.label: NARRATOR'S DESCRIPTION; EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: The Prophet ﷺ liked beginning with the right in appropriate actions, including cleanliness and dressing.
lessons.explanation: Beautiful manners can become part of your everyday routine, one thoughtful action at a time.
lessons.action: Begin a suitable daily action, such as putting on clothes, with the right side.
lessons.story: Imaan is getting dressed for Eid. She remembers to put her right arm into her sleeve first. It is a small thing, but it reminds her to follow the Sunnah throughout her day.
lessons.question: You are putting on your clothes. Which side could you begin with?

answers.text: The right side.
answers.feedback: Beautiful manners can be part of your everyday routine.

answers.text: Whichever is quickest.
answers.feedback: There is a beautiful Sunnah for this. Try again.

answers.text: The left side always.
answers.feedback: Think again. Which side did the Prophet ﷺ like to begin with?

lessons.title: Yawn Politely
lessons.arabic: فَإِذَا تَثَاوَبَ أَحَدُكُمْ فَلْيَرُدَّهُ مَا اسْتَطَاعَ
lessons.label: EXCERPT; COVERING MOUTH ALSO TAUGHT IN RELATED AUTHENTIC REPORTS
lessons.meaning: Try to restrain a yawn as much as reasonably possible, according to the Hadith.
lessons.explanation: Even small public manners show care for others. You can keep your behavior polite when you are tired.
lessons.action: When you yawn today, cover your mouth and behave quietly.
lessons.story: In a quiet assembly, Akhlaq feels a big yawn coming. He tries to hold it back and covers his mouth with his hand. He stays quiet so others are not disturbed.
lessons.question: You feel a yawn coming in a quiet place. What is polite?

answers.text: Yawn loudly with your mouth wide open.
answers.feedback: Small public manners show care for others. Try again.

answers.text: Try to hold it back and cover your mouth.
answers.feedback: You kept your behaviour polite, even when tired.

answers.text: Make a funny noise while yawning.
answers.feedback: That might disturb others. Think again.

lessons.title: Make Salam a Friendly Habit
lessons.arabic: يُسَلِّمُ الرَّاكِبُ عَلَى الْمَاشِي وَالْمَاشِي عَلَى الْقَاعِدِ
lessons.label: EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: The Sunnah teaches considerate ways of initiating greetings in different situations.
lessons.explanation: You can be the person who starts a friendly greeting. It spreads warmth without costing anything.
lessons.action: When you approach a seated family member today, begin with a respectful Salam.
lessons.story: Imaan walks into the living room where Dadi Jaan is sitting. Before asking for anything, she begins with a respectful, “Assalamu Alaikum, Dadi Jaan.” Dadi Jaan replies with a warm smile.
lessons.question: You walk up to a family member who is sitting down. What could you do first?

answers.text: Begin with a respectful salam.
answers.feedback: Starting a friendly greeting spreads warmth without costing anything.

answers.text: Start asking for things right away.
answers.feedback: There is a lovely way to begin. Try again.

answers.text: Wait for them to greet you first.
answers.feedback: You can be the one who begins. Think again.

lessons.title: Use Gentle Hands
lessons.arabic: مَا ضَرَبَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ شَيْئًا قَطُّ بِيَدِهِ وَلَا امْرَأَةً وَلَا خَادِمًا
lessons.label: NARRATOR'S DESCRIPTION; EXCERPT
lessons.meaning: A'ishah رضي الله عنها described that the Prophet ﷺ did not strike women or servants, reflecting his gentle conduct.
lessons.explanation: Your hands can help, build, comfort, and protect. When you are upset, choose safe and gentle actions.
lessons.action: During one frustrating moment today, keep your hands gentle and use words to ask for help.
lessons.story: Akhlaq is building a puzzle, and his little sister keeps taking pieces. He feels frustrated and his hands want to snatch them back. He keeps his hands gentle and says, “Please can you give them back? Ammi, can you help us?”
lessons.question: You feel frustrated with someone. What could your hands do?

answers.text: Hit or push them.
answers.feedback: Hitting can hurt. Your hands can be gentle even when you are upset.

answers.text: Snatch things from them.
answers.feedback: Snatching can hurt or scare someone. Try again.

answers.text: Stay gentle and use words to ask for help.
answers.feedback: Your hands can help, build, comfort and protect.
